name: Dr. Joshua Miele
description: Photo of Josh Miele, a white man with curly brown hair. He has a blue left eye and scars covering his face and right eye. He is smiling at the camera and wearing a blue sweater. He is outside with greenery in the background.
bio: Dr. Joshua Miele has been a creative leader in the area of blindness accessibility for over thirty years. He is a respected member of the blind community with significant contributions to such technologies as screen readers, auditory displays, audio/tactile maps and graphics, wayfinding, braille input, and video description. His work is characterized by the imaginative use of low-cost, mainstream technologies to address significant challenges in information accessibility. name: Charity Pitcher-Cooper
description: Photo of Charity Pitcher-Cooper, a light skinned woman with long brown hair with heavy bangs smiles warmly from her home office. She wears a headset with a microphone, and her chin rests casually on her hand.
bio: Charity Pitcher-Cooper is passionate about making online video more accessible for blind and low vision audiences through community-driven audio description. She has trained and mentored hundreds of volunteer audio describers and guided graduate students in accessible user interface design and disability-centered development. Charity also helped lead the creation of the YuWA dataset, a public archive of audio description data supporting research in accessibility, artificial intelligence, and inclusive media. Her work focuses on ensuring that accessibility remains collaborative, practical, and centered on the experiences of blind and low vision communities.

name: Dr. Ilmi Yoon
bio: Dr. Ilmi Yoon is a Teaching Professor and Director of Computing Programs at Khoury College of Computer Sciences, Northeastern University's Silicon Valley campus, which she joined in 2024 after more than two decades at San Francisco State University. Dr. Yoon's research focuses on human-centered AI, video accessibility, and socially responsible computing, with a commitment to increasing participation in computing among underrepresented communities. She started YouDescribe collaboration in 2016, and launched the development of YouDescribeX (the AI-enhanced version) with multiple contributors including Drs. Fazli, Ihorn, Siu, and Das, along with her students listed here. She has served as PI/Co-PI on multiple NSF grants focused on Computer Science Education and diversity in computing.
